Trump's newest round of global tariffs backs up his administration's committed belief that trade is a national emergency. 

The latest duties will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and are coming into force at the end of a months-long investigation focused on the issue of forced labor.

$INTC popped after the company reported a blowout earnings win on Thursday after the bell. 

CEO Lip-Bu Tan declared "Q2 was another quarter of solid execution" on the company's earnings call. yhoo.it/4vODoV9

The Trump administration announced new global tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on many top trading partners, replacing rates set to expire at midnight.

Trump's trade office said in a fact sheet that this order will apply to 60 of the top US trade partners and cover 99.4% of US imports.

Intel is raising its capex spending plans for 2026 to more than $20 billion — far more than they estimated going into the year, CFO David Zinsner said on the company's Q2 earnings call. 

The company also expects for 2027's capex spend to be "significantly above" its 2026 levels.

Intel CFO Dave Zinsner says the company is upping its 2026 capex spend, and estimates 2027 spend will be even higher.

"We're raising our outlook for 2026 and now expect our CapEx to be more than $20 billion, which is up significantly versus our expectations entering the year."
